pageInfo.subtitle: Master the advanced arpeggio technique that creates fluid, cascading runs through coordinated picking and fretting motions.
pageInfo.heroDescription: Sweep picking is an advanced guitar technique that creates flowing arpeggio passages through coordinated pick strokes across multiple strings. By "sweeping" the pick in one continuous motion while precisely timing the fretting hand, guitarists can achieve lightning-fast arpeggios with incredible fluidity and a distinctive cascading sound that's essential for neo-classical, metal, and fusion styles.

items.text: Maintain consistent pick angle and depth
Keep pick strokes flowing in one direction
Use economy of motion - no wasted movement
Practice both ascending and descending sweeps
Time finger placement precisely with pick
Release previous notes to avoid muddiness
Use rolling finger motions for bar chords
Maintain light but secure finger pressure

exercises.title: Two-String Sweep Exercises
exercises.description: Start with simple two-string sweeps to develop the basic motion and coordination. Focus on smooth pick movement and precise timing between hands.

patternNote.text: Motion: Down-down for ascending, up-up for descending

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use continuous downstrokes for ascending patterns and continuous upstrokes for descending. The pick should flow smoothly across strings without stopping. Start very slowly.

exercises.title: Three-String Arpeggio Sweeps
exercises.description: Extend to three-string arpeggios using basic triad shapes. This is where sweep picking really starts to sound musical and distinctive.

patternNote.text: Pattern: A minor triad arpeggio across three strings

notation.title: A Minor Triad: Three-String Sweep Arpeggios

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Focus on clean note separation - each note should ring clearly without bleeding into the next. Practice the fretting hand motion separately before adding the pick sweep.

exercises.title: Five-String Arpeggio Sweeps
exercises.description: Master the classic five-string sweep pattern that forms the foundation of most sweep picking applications. This creates the full, flowing arpeggio sound.

patternNote.text: Pattern: A minor arpeggio across five strings (6th to 2nd)

notation.title: A Minor Five-String Sweep: Ascending and Descending

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: This is the classic sweep picking pattern. Practice the ascending sweep with continuous downstrokes, then the descending with continuous upstrokes. Keep the motion fluid.

exercises.title: Six-String Full Sweeps
exercises.description: Extend sweep picking across all six strings for maximum dramatic effect. This technique is commonly used in neo-classical and metal genres for impressive arpeggio runs.

patternNote.text: Challenge: Maintain fluidity across all six strings

notation.title: A Minor Six-String Sweep: Full Range Arpeggio

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: This is the most challenging sweep pattern. Break it down into smaller sections first, then connect them. Pay special attention to the turnaround on the high E string.

exercises.title: Sweep + Tap Combinations
exercises.description: Combine sweep picking with tapping techniques to create extended arpeggios that span multiple octaves. This advanced technique creates spectacular musical effects.

patternNote.text: Technique: Sweep followed by two-handed tapping extension

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Master the basic sweep first, then add the tapping extension. The transition between swept notes and tapped notes should be seamless and musical.

exercises.title: Various Chord Types
exercises.description: Apply sweep picking to different chord qualities - major, minor, diminished, and augmented. This expands your harmonic vocabulary and musical applications.

patternNote.text: Progression: Am - C - F - G sweep arpeggios on strings 4-3-2

notation.title: Chord Progression: Am - C - F - G Swept Arpeggios

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Practice each chord type separately first, then work on smooth transitions between different arpeggio shapes. This creates musical chord progressions with sweep picking.

exercises.title: Diminished Arpeggio Sweeps
exercises.description: Diminished arpeggios are staples of neo-classical guitar and create dramatic, exotic-sounding passages. Their symmetrical nature makes them perfect for sweep picking.

patternNote.text: Theory: Diminished 7th arpeggio with minor-third intervals

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Diminished arpeggios repeat every three frets, so you can play this same pattern starting from frets 6, 9, 12, etc. Great for creating tension in solos.

exercises.title: Speed Development Drill
exercises.description: Progressive speed building exercise combining multiple sweep patterns for developing the lightning-fast arpeggios heard in professional neo-classical and metal playing.

patternNote.text: Goal: Continuous sweep patterns at high speed with perfect clarity

notation.title: Connected Sweep Patterns for Speed Building

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use progressive tempo training: start at 60 BPM, increase by 5 BPM every successful repetition. Focus on maintaining perfect note clarity at all speeds.

items.title: Technical Development
items: Always start with two-string sweeps before advancing
Practice fretting hand motion separately from picking
Focus on note clarity before attempting speed
Record yourself to identify timing and coordination issues
Practice with different pick materials and techniques

challenges.title: Muddy Sound
challenges.text: Usually caused by poor muting technique. Practice lifting previous fingers to stop unwanted ringing between notes.

challenges.title: Uneven Timing
challenges.text: Focus on coordinating both hands precisely. Practice with a metronome and isolate difficult transitions.

challenges.title: Pick Getting Stuck
challenges.text: Use lighter pick attack and ensure smooth motion. Practice the picking motion on muted strings first.

items.reason: Fast thin neck and low action make sweep picking arpeggios much easier to execute cleanly
Rigid, pointed picks glide smoothly across strings for clean sweep movements
